summary: Firetrack turns NASA FIRMS active fire hotspots from four satellites (Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP and NOAA-20) into one monthly burning activity calendar that can be compared from November 2000 to today. Raw hotspot counts jump every time a new sensor joins: in Spain the raw count rises about 200% from 2011 to 2013 only because VIIRS starts, while Aqua alone goes down. We calibrate VIIRS against Aqua MODIS month by month, clip every detection to the official boundary of the area, and show the result as a calendar with anomalies, yearly totals, validation and CSV downloads. The demo covers Spain and Aragón, the region of our local event, where 2026 stands out as the most active summer of the whole record.
details:
What it does

Firetrack builds a harmonized monthly fire activity index for an area of interest and shows it as a calendar (months by years). Each cell is one month in Aqua MODIS equivalent hotspots, so 2005 and 2024 can be read on the same scale. The user can switch to an anomaly view (each month against the median of the same calendar month), see yearly totals and the seasonal profile, read which satellite carried each month and with which factor, and download the detections behind the view as CSV.

How it works

1. Ingest: we read NASA FIRMS detections (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m) from a public GeoParquet mirror with DuckDB, by bounding box and year. We checked the mirror against the official FIRMS country files for 2016 and 2022 and the counts are identical.

2. Clean: we keep vegetation fires only (static sources removed), MODIS confidence 30 or more and VIIRS not low, and clip every detection to the official boundary (Spain mainland and Balearic Islands, and Aragón).

3. Calibrate: one VIIRS to Aqua factor per calendar month, measured on the overlap years and shrunk toward the yearly factor when a month has few detections. Terra bridges 2000 to 2002, NOAA-20 fills the tail after Suomi-NPP. Aragón has too few detections for its own seasonal shape, so its monthly factors borrow the shape of Spain.

4. Validate: a blind test refits the factors on 2012 to 2016 only, hides Aqua and rebuilds 2017 to 2020 from VIIRS alone. Error: Spain +7.8% (raw VIIRS +592%), Aragón -16.7% (raw VIIRS +477%). Month ranking is kept (Spearman 0.94 in Spain).

5. Serve: the pipeline writes static JSON and CSV files that the web app reads directly, so it needs no server. A FastAPI service serves the same payloads for other uses. A GitHub Actions workflow rebuilds the data and opens a pull request when the pipeline changes.

Benefits

Fire managers, scientists and emergency teams get a record where a change means more or less fire, not a new camera. It shows which months are unusual for an area and how this year compares with 25 years of history, with honest limits: the index is not a count of fires, and partial or provisional months are flagged.

Tools

Python, DuckDB, pandas, NumPy, FastAPI, Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, GitHub Actions.
